rewrites.//: Every path is a client route and must reach index.html, since the router lives in the browser and the server has no such pages. Everything except /assets: those are the built JavaScript and CSS files, named after a hash of their contents, and a deployment renames all of them. Sending a request for one that no longer exists to index.html answered it with a page of HTML at 200 OK, and a browser expecting a JavaScript module made what it could of that - which is a rendering error on a working application whose only fault was being one version behind. Excluded, a name that has gone returns 404, which is what it is.
